text:
$$\exists K\ \forall n,k\in\mathbb{N}:\quad K<k,\ \ 2k\le n<k^2,\ \ 2\mid k,\ \ k\equiv 2 \pmod 3,\ \ n\equiv 2 \pmod 3,\ \ k \bmod q \le n \bmod q\ (q=5,7,11,13) \implies \exists\,p\le k \text{ prime with } n \bmod p < k \bmod p$$

For all large even $k$ with $k\equiv 2 \pmod 3$, every $n$ with $2k\le n<k^2$, $n\equiv 2 \pmod 3$, and residue mod $q$ at least that of $k$ for each of $q=5,7,11,13$, has a prime $p\le k$ whose residue of $n$ is smaller than its residue of $k$. Lean writes the residue hypotheses as `k % 3 = 2`, `n % 3 = 2` and `k % q ≤ n % q`, and $k^2$ as `k * k`. `n % p` is the least non-negative residue, so the condition reads $n \bmod p < k \bmod p$, a carry at the last base-$p$ digit when $k$ is subtracted from $n$ (hence $p \mid \binom{n}{k}$ by Kummer's theorem, though the statement names no binomial coefficient).
label: Residue form, k even, k ≡ n ≡ 2 (mod 3), no carry 5 to 13
